texts.preamble: Shri Kumar T.N vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co on 2 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: This the 2nd day of April 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.2609/2018 Petitioner Shri Kumar T.N., Son of Nanjaiah @ Nanjappa, Aged about 52 years, Resident of No.195, Adakamaranahalli, Makali, Bengaluru Rural District-562 123. (By Pleader Shri R.Chandra Shekar) V/s. Respondents 1.Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd., No.89, Svr Complex, Ii floor, Madivala, Hosur Road, Bengaluru-560 068. (Policy No.3001/MI-04805757/00/000 valid from 17.7.2017 to 16.7.2018) (By Pleader Shri H.G.Srinivas) 2 Scch-18 Mvc 2609/2018 2.Shri Basavaraj H., Son of Hosalappa, No.147, Madanayakanahalli, Bengaluru-562 123. (Exparte) J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.6,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road Shri Kumar T.N vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co on 2 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102605033/ 1 traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 18.1.2018 at about 9.00 p.m. the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-52-L-7220 on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-4 service road from his place towards Nelamangala, when he reached near Ravathanahalli gate, a car bearing No.KA-32-M-5495 driven by its driver came from Dasanapura side towards Ravuthanahalli gate side in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle. Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately he was shifted to VP Magnus Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he was treated as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 52 years, Security Guard and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-32-M-5495. Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement and the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and placed exparte. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further this respondent has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No. KA-32-M- 5495 and its validity. 7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P14 to Ex.P18. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
texts.arguments: Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars. Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same. Further contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost. Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has denied the accident in toto, hence, prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.1. The counsel for the respondent No.1 has argued that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle i.e., the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the car. On the other hand petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence. 17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 25. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 52 years, working as a security guard and getting an income of Rs.15,000/- per month. Due to the accident, he is getting pain in his shoulder, not able to sleep on his left side and not able to lift weight with his left hand and not able to drive/or ride any vehicle. the petitioner has produced x-ray marked at Ex.P13. The petitioner has not examine the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability. Therefore, no amount is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of future earning. 26. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries, so his happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out his life.
